annotationRationale: The solution finds all allowed factor pairs and compares their perimeters to establish an attained minimum. Prime factorization makes the list exhaustive, while rectangle area and perimeter formulas connect the factors to the geometry.
sourceMethod: Follows the official factor-pair comparison, adding a prime factorization and a bound on the shorter side to justify completeness.

review.mathCheck: The factorization \(2024=2^3\cdot11\cdot23\) gives exactly the listed eight shorter-side possibilities. The four smallest give perimeters above 400; the remaining perimeters are 390, 228, 222 and 180. Thus the minimum is \(180\), choice B, matching the key.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Originally worded, faithful adaptation of MAA Q6 on page 3: the same exhaustive factor-pair comparison, with factorization and the shorter-side cutoff explicitly justifying completeness.
review.annotationCheck: The enumeration covers every positive integer rectangle once. The explanation is reconstructible at AMC 10 level; no figure or additional method is needed.
